To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the perceived limitation that obesity may have on TLRR for locally advance disease was not demonstrated.
obesity does not appear to have any significant impact on perioperative outcomes, margin status or lymph node harvest.
obese patients undergoing TLRR for T3/T4 rectal cancer had similar operative times, blood loss, conversion rates, lymph node retrieval and margin positivity as normal-weight and overweight patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the feasibility of laparoscopic resections for obese patients with locally advanced rectal tumors.
the feasibility of totally laparoscopic resections for locally advanced rectals tumors.
the feasibility of laparoscopic rectal resection in obese patients with rectum cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TLRR is a feasible option for the obese patient with rectal cancer.
TLRR for locally-advanced rectal cancer can be performed with acceptable outcomes and oncologic efficacy in the obese patient.

obese patients undergoing laparoscopic rectal resection for locally advanced rectals cancer have similar oncologic outcomes and perioperative complications to normal-weight and overweight patients, and therefore should be offered TLRR as the primary surgical approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obesity does not preclude the use of TLRR in the setting of locally advanced disease.
TLRR is safe for patients with rectal cancers, regardless of body mass index.
the laparoscopic approach to rectal cancer resections in obese patients is feasible with similar perioperative and oncological outcomes to non-obese patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TLRR is feasible and safe in the setting of obesity and locally advanced rectal disease.
obese patients should not be excluded from TLRR based on their body habitus alone.
TLRR is technically feasible in patients with locally advanced rectal tumors and obesity should not be a limiting factor in the decision to perform this operation.
